findings.issue: This link is not in scope for the era-5 pass. Both ends are era-6 movements (franciscan-order-era-6, 1300-1517; observant-reform-and-popular-preaching, 1368-1517). The launch prompt allows a link to another era only 'when this era's movement is the one whose text names it'. That rule admits links with one end in era 5. It does not admit a link between two movements of a later era. The era-6 order's own summary names 'the Observant wing' as one of its branches, so P2-L6 will inventory this pair. Drawing it now changes the converged plan without a change order. The error started in round 1: R1-07 proposed this exact pair. The link itself is sound. Its two quotes match lines 34646-34648 and 34650-34653, and the reviser was right to drop the preface locus (191-192) as editorial. Would a different pair carry the era-5 claim better? Yes, but not as 'gave rise to'. A the-franciscan-movement --gave rise to--> observant-reform-and-popular-preaching link would be anachronistic: the era-5 movement ends in 1300, the Observance starts at Brugliano in 1368, and no named person passes from one to the other. 'Influenced' on that pair is Documented in the same vendored volume, because the later side names the earlier side's work, the Rule of Francis. Eugenius IV's letter of 28 August 1440 (no. 485) speaks of friars Minor at a hermitage in the diocese of Astorga living 'sub observantia regulae beati Francisci'. The era-5 sentence then needs to say what that link shows. 'Grew up later inside the same order' is a claim about the era-6 order, and the era-6 order's own text already carries it.

findings.issue: These phrases describe the project's library, not the evidence. The era-3 review (R1-14, R2-05, R3) ruled them internal language, and Open-Gaps 40 logs the same fault in an era-2 note. Round 1 missed them and itself proposed this wording in R1-01, R1-03, R1-05, R1-06 and R1-17. The revision kept that wording and added one more in the new Observant note. The era-3 cure ('No source from the time...') would be wrong for several of these. For Serbian and Bulgarian hesychasm, for the Fetha Nagast and for the Kyivan chronicle, sources of the time do exist; they are only not vendored. To say none exists would be a new false claim. So each replacement below says what the cited source does or does not show, or that the source behind it is not quoted. None of them claims that no source exists. One fix applied once is the root-cause fix, so the unchanged era-5 instances are listed too.
